title: Delivering Better for Chicago
body: Dion's Chicago Dream believes nutritious food should be a lived reality, not an aspiration, and has built the infrastructure to prove it: 325,000 pounds of fresh produce moved monthly to more than 5,400 households a week across every Chicago neighborhood. The Dream Box extends that reliability to the last few feet of the journey.

feature.title: Their product. Our platform.
feature.body: The Dream Box is Dion's Chicago Dream's own product, built on Veranda's platform. It lives on a stoop or at a community site with no power, Wi-Fi, or installer required, running on battery over long-range wireless. Insulated and sensor-equipped, it keeps produce fresh, admits only the authorized carrier, and flags anything out of the ordinary — so a delivery that reaches the block also reaches the family behind it.

points.title: The challenge
points.body: Fresh food arrives on a schedule, but the households receiving it often can't be home to meet it. A doorstep drop risks spoilage and theft; a missed one means another trip.

points.title: How it fits
points.body: The Dream Box slots into the program's existing routes. Carriers are verified automatically, and the program sees what has arrived, its condition, and who has access.

points.title: Intended value
points.body: For the organization: fewer failed drops and less waste. For households: fresh food that's there when they get home — closing the gap between a meal grown and a meal received.
